sites.tag_type: short epitope, ALFA 15 aa, GS linkers
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: cAMP-responsive luciferase assay (PMC6155907): pEC50 8.8 ± 0.1 (myc-tagged) vs 8.3 ± 0.1 (WT), not significantly different. SNAP-tagged constructs (PMC5913239, PMC12808597): appropriate cAMP responses to agonist stimulation confirmed. Surface expression confirmed by FACS (LUXendin) and ELISA (PMC11610247).
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1–23 (topology landmarks, authoritative). The mature N-terminus begins at residue 24 (R). Inserting a tag after residue 23 places it between P (pos 23, last residue of the cleaved signal peptide) and R (pos 24, first residue of the mature extracellular domain). Python confirmed: seq[22]='P', seq[23]='R'. The junction is 120 residues from TM1 (144–168), providing ample extracellular space. The myc-tag paper (PMC6155907) explicitly states 'immediately downstream of the putative signal peptide' for a full-length membrane-anchored construct, and the functional assay shows preserved potency. Four additional independent papers (PMC5913239, PMC12808597, PMC11610247, PMC13267291) all place SNAP-tags or SNAP/FLAG combinations at the same N-terminal position of full-length GLP-1R with confirmed surface expression and cAMP function. All C-terminal tag entries in the ledger (YFP, FLAG, Strep-tag II, nanoluciferase) map to the intracellular C-terminus (residues 406–463, topology INTRACELLULAR) and are disqualified. The L260 amber-stop construct (PMC9917595) targets an intracellular loop (topology 250–267, INTRACELLULAR) and is disqualified. [validation: surface_and_function; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: Introduction of a myc-tag to the N-terminus of GLP-1R immediately downstream of the putative signal peptide did not significantly affect the potency of GLP-1 at this receptor when assessed using a cAMP-responsive luciferase assay ( Figure 1 ).
